A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SEMA and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original continual-learning experiments on four datasets, with ablations, runtime measurements, low-data experiments, and repeated-run results.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds experiments with longer task sequences, additional baselines, RanPAC enhancement, and CLIP.

M1.justification: Appendix C.10 introduces SEMA+RanPAC, applying random-projection feature enhancement and prototype classification to SEMA representations. This adds a composed variant; the core adapter, representation descriptor, router, objectives, and self-expansion procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-100, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-A, and VTAB for class-incremental learning, including the same low-data subsets. Additional task splits, CLIP weights, and representation enhancement change experimental configurations without adding datasets or downstream tasks.

E2.justification: v3 substantially broadens the evaluated comparisons: InfLoRA joins Tables 1 and 4 and incremental-performance plots; Table 14 compares SEMA+RanPAC against RanPAC; Table 15 introduces zero-shot CLIP alongside ADAM. RanPAC was cited but not evaluated in v2. Finetune Adapter and FT Adapter are the same retained comparator.

E3.justification: v3 adds 5-task ImageNet-R evaluations with 40 classes per task, 50-task ImageNet-R/ImageNet-A evaluations with four classes per task, and CLIP and RanPAC-enhanced configurations. These substantially extend the evaluation design. The 10-task ImageNet-R/ImageNet-A evaluations already existed in v2's appendix.

E4.justification: v3 extends task-length sensitivity checks and the router-versus-RD comparison to additional splits, and adds a focused test of compatibility with RanPAC enhancement. The extensive existing expansion, routing, threshold, layer, adapter-type, low-data, and AE-width analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 Table 13 adds uncertainty for the previously reported 10-task ImageNet-R result: final accuracy is 78.00 ± 0.49, whereas v2 Table 10 reported 78.00 without uncertainty. Both versions specify five independent runs with varying seeds, class orders, and initialization; an increase in run count is not established.

E6.justification: Matched original scores remain unchanged, but v3 adds substantial results for new comparators and configurations. Its 50-task final accuracies are 67.03 on ImageNet-R and 49.18 on ImageNet-A. The added InfLoRA comparison also changes the ranking in Table 4: on 20-task ImageNet-R with IN21K weights, InfLoRA scores 69.65 versus SEMA's retained 69.60.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, Equations 1–4, and z-score rule remain equivalent; neither version presents theorems or proofs. v3 removes B.3's unused standard forgetting-metric formula, an explanatory deletion rather than a revision to theoretical reasoning or an evaluated metric.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same central claims: demand-driven adapter expansion, knowledge reuse, sub-linear parameter growth, and competitive rehearsal-free continual learning. Additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 3.4 now explicitly acknowledges that freezing existing router parameters restricts but cannot eliminate forgetting. Appendix C.10 explains complementarity with RanPAC's feature enhancement, while C.1 qualifies outperformance as applying to most settings. The original online-learning and RD-related limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a SEMA code-access link, adapter hidden dimension 16, a 500-sample reconstruction-error buffer, and further baseline and scanning details. These are additional disclosures, not established implementation changes. Conversely, it omits v2's explicit training budgets of five adapter epochs and twenty RD epochs.

R1.justification: v3 expands the PTM-based related-work discussion with works including InfLoRA, ConvPrompt, CLAP4CLIP, and CLIP. It also positions SEMA as complementary to the already-cited RanPAC. The broader continual-learning and parameter-efficient adaptation positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 polishes grammar and terminology throughout, revises some headings and explanations, updates author affiliations, and reorganizes the supplementary experiment subsections. The main narrative and section sequence remain substantially the same.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column layout throughout, redraws Figure 2 with explicit expansion and reuse cases, expands comparison tables, and converts v2's 10-task result tables into Figure 12 curves. Figure 12 introduces incorrect class-count axes: its ten-class tick increments conflict with the stated 40- or 20-class task splits.

improvement.justification: The InfLoRA comparisons, longer-sequence tests, and RanPAC/CLIP experiments strengthen support for SEMA's competitiveness and applicability. The explicit router limitation and added implementation details also improve clarity. These gains outweigh limited reporting regressions, particularly the omitted epoch budgets and incorrect Figure 12 class-count axes; the already extensive core evidence remains largely unchanged.
